codon.ui.help.start.title: Start debugging
codon.ui.help.start.body: Aim at a command block and press %s to toggle its breakpoint, then trigger the command normally. When execution pauses, press %s to switch between the cursor and the world. Choose a context, inspect its values, then step or continue. Opening or closing the debugger does not resume execution.
codon.ui.help.breakpoints.title: Block and function breakpoints
codon.ui.help.breakpoints.body: Use /codon breakpoint block <x> <y> <z> or /codon breakpoint function <function> <line> to toggle a breakpoint. Function lines start at 1. Use /codon breakpoint list to see active breakpoints, or /codon breakpoint clear to remove them all. Debugger commands require command permissions.
codon.ui.help.session.title: Paused, running, or finished?
codon.ui.help.session.body: The header shows the execution state. Paused means you can inspect and step; Waiting for server means a control request is in progress. Finished lets you inspect final values before continuing. Recorded commands can remain visible while Running, but step controls are disabled.
codon.ui.help.stop.title: World marker colors
codon.ui.help.stop.body: Orange (amber) marks the currently stopped command block, with a point at its center. Other block breakpoints have red outlines. Teal shows execution anchors and facing. Green and red context markers describe branches in execute flow; they do not mean entities were created or deleted.
codon.ui.help.camera.title: Move around while paused
codon.ui.help.camera.body: Close this guide, then use %s to switch between the cursor and freecam. Move with %s / %s / %s / %s, go up / down with %s / %s, and move faster with %s. Freecam moves your viewpoint without moving the player. Key labels follow your bindings in Options > Controls > Key Binds.
codon.ui.help.keep_freecam.title: Keep freecam while running
codon.ui.help.keep_freecam.body: Use the camera toggle beside Information or press %s in the debugger or world to keep freecam after continuing. The world and player resume normally while your movement controls still move only the camera. Turn it off while running to return to the player. This preference is saved across worlds and restarts.
codon.ui.help.hide_ui.title: Hide the debugger
codon.ui.help.hide_ui.body: Tap %s to toggle debugger panels and markers. Hold for at least 250 ms to hide them only while pressed, then restore the previous visibility. The game HUD, chat, scoreboard, and action bar stay visible. Hidden panels cannot be clicked, and execution stays in its current state. Opening another screen or leaving the window resets visibility.
codon.ui.help.control.resume: Continue execution until another breakpoint is reached or execution finishes. At the final-value inspection stop, continue to release the pause.
codon.ui.help.control.over: Advance to the next command stage at the same or a shallower call depth, stepping over nested function execution.
codon.ui.help.control.into: Pause at the next command stage, including stages inside a called function. One step is a command stage, not a game tick.
codon.ui.help.control.out: Run until execution returns to a shallower call depth. At the outermost level, stop when execution completes. Hold Ctrl with your current Step Into binding; this also follows custom bindings.
codon.ui.help.availability.title: Execution shortcuts
codon.ui.help.availability.body: Use these buttons or shortcuts while paused, after closing this guide. Controls are disabled while a request is pending. The action always controls the actual paused execution, even when you are inspecting an older command.
codon.ui.help.keyboard.title: Navigate with the keyboard
codon.ui.help.keyboard.body: In the debugger, %s moves between containers such as the toolbar, Contexts, NBT, and Watches. %s moves within the current container; it stays there at the end of a list. Use %s to activate the focused button. In watch forms, Tab moves between fields.
codon.ui.help.scrolling.title: Read long lists and commands
codon.ui.help.scrolling.body: Scroll over the panel you want to browse. In the debugger, click a scrollbar track or drag its thumb to move through contexts, NBT, watches, or command content. In this guide, use the wheel, Up/Down, Page Up/Down, or Home/End; Left/Right selects a tab button and Enter opens it.
codon.ui.help.gizmo.title: Group nearby context labels
codon.ui.help.gizmo.body: The gizmo button switches between Grouped and Labels. In Grouped mode, nearby contexts share a label. A +N suffix counts additional contexts in that group. Click it to open the group in Contexts, choose a member to inspect, or use All to return to the full list.
codon.ui.help.labels.title: Individual labels and crowded scenes
codon.ui.help.labels.body: Labels mode shows separate context labels where space permits. Click one to select its context; its number matches the inspector entry. At most 20 labels are shown at once, so crowded scenes can still combine contexts into +N groups. Use the Contexts list to inspect individual entries.
codon.ui.help.details.title: Show or hide the inspector
codon.ui.help.details.body: The Details button shows or hides Contexts, the selected context details, and its entity NBT. Watches keeps saved fields available separately. The command panel below the world contains execute flow and the call stack; expand it to read longer commands.
codon.ui.help.opacity.title: Adjust panel opacity
codon.ui.help.opacity.body: Drag the small slider in the Codon header, or focus it and use %s. It fades panel backgrounds and borders from 0 to 100 percent. Text, icons and keyboard focus stay readable. The header stays visible so you can restore opacity. This setting is saved across worlds and restarts.
codon.ui.help.source.title: What is an execution context?
codon.ui.help.source.body: A context is the executor, position, dimension, and facing used by a command. It can represent an entity or just a position. Select it in the list or through a world label to inspect it. Selection changes what you inspect without moving the entity or rerunning the command.
codon.ui.help.coordinates.title: Read position and facing
codon.ui.help.coordinates.body: Details shows the recorded execution anchor as X / Y / Z and facing as yaw / pitch. The anchor can differ from the entity position. When a recorded parent context is available, an arrow row shows previous values for changed fields; a dash means that field did not change.
codon.ui.help.move_camera.title: Move the camera to a context
codon.ui.help.move_camera.body: Click the camera icon in context details to move the freecam eye to the selected recorded anchor and match its facing. This requires a pause, an active freecam, and a context in your dimension. It moves only the camera. Distant terrain may not be loaded while paused; hover a disabled icon for the reason.
codon.ui.help.created.title: Context created (+)
codon.ui.help.created.body: Green marks an execution context created by a branching stage, such as execute as. It does not mean an entity was summoned.
codon.ui.help.changed.title: Context changed (↗)
codon.ui.help.changed.body: Purple marks a context whose executor, position, dimension, or facing changed at this stage. The previous values appear below the current values in Details.
codon.ui.help.excluded.title: Context removed (-)
codon.ui.help.excluded.body: Red marks a context removed from the execution flow by this stage. That branch does not continue. It does not mean an entity was deleted.
codon.ui.help.offscreen.title: Outside the visible world
codon.ui.help.offscreen.body: The outside-viewport icon means the selected context is outside the visible world area or in another dimension. Check its dimension and anchor in Details. A missing world label does not mean the context or entity was removed.
codon.ui.help.uuid.title: Copy an executor UUID
codon.ui.help.uuid.body: Click the copy icon in context details to copy the entity executor UUID. You can use it as a fixed watch target. Position-only contexts have no entity UUID.
codon.ui.help.flow.title: Inspect an execute stage
codon.ui.help.flow.body: Click a recorded clause in the command panel to inspect that stage, its contexts, and world markers. Amber marks the actual stopped clause; teal marks the clause you are inspecting. Unobserved text has no recorded counts. Selecting a stage only changes the inspection view.
codon.ui.help.counts.title: Contexts, runs, and successes
codon.ui.help.counts.body: Input → output counts show how many execution contexts enter and leave a stage. Runs counts command executions; Successes counts successful executions. These are separate from the number of contexts. An ellipsis (...) means a value was not measured; 0 means it was measured as zero.
codon.ui.help.recording.title: Incomplete recording
codon.ui.help.recording.body: A warning icon means some execution details were not recorded. Hover it for the reason, such as a detail limit, an unfinished stage, or missing input/output links. Counts and visible branches may describe only part of the execution; missing data is not proof that nothing happened.
codon.ui.help.history.title: Browse recorded execution
codon.ui.help.history.body: Use the previous/next controls to browse retained execution. Where execution order was recorded, navigation follows function calls and returns. Up to 64 command flow records are retained. Inspecting history does not rewind the world. Current returns to the actual stopped command and its live call stack.
codon.ui.help.stack.title: Follow the call stack
codon.ui.help.stack.body: The call stack belongs to the command being inspected and can include functions that have already returned. Click a frame to inspect its caller while keeping that stack available. Scroll horizontally over the call path, use the wheel, or drag its scrollbar to browse frames. Stack not recorded means those frames are unavailable.
codon.ui.help.watch.title: Add or edit a watch
codon.ui.help.watch.body: Click + beside Watches, choose a type, and type or browse its target and path. The form previews values while paused. Enter adds the watch; Ctrl+Enter adds it and keeps the form open. Open Watch to edit, pin, inspect, or remove saved entries.
codon.ui.help.types.title: Choose what to watch
codon.ui.help.types.body: Score reads a scoreboard objective. Entity NBT reads an entity path such as Health. Storage NBT reads a storage ID such as example:state and a path. Leave the optional target blank to follow the selected entity context, or choose a fixed target. Storage uses its own ID instead of an executor.
codon.ui.help.score_holders.title: Watch fake players and named scores
codon.ui.help.score_holders.body: For Score, the optional target accepts an entity UUID or a score-holder name, such as #total. Choose can browse entities and existing score holders. A named holder does not need an entity. Quote a name containing spaces, or a UUID-shaped name that should be treated as a literal score holder.
codon.ui.help.pin.title: Follow context or keep a fixed target
codon.ui.help.pin.body: An unbound Score or Entity NBT watch follows the selected live entity context. Use its pin to keep reading that entity as you switch contexts. A named score holder is also a fixed target. Unpin either kind to follow the selected entity again. Storage NBT keeps its storage ID.
codon.ui.help.grouping.title: Organize Watches
codon.ui.help.grouping.body: Use Group by to organize entries by Context, Path, or No group. Context groups share a target; Path groups share an objective or NBT path. Storage entries stay together by storage ID. Pinned watches take priority, while unchanged missing values move to the end of their group. Grouping changes only the display.
codon.ui.help.values.title: Read values and read errors
codon.ui.help.values.body: Each entry shows its field and displayed value, with its target or binding below. Amber arrows show changes; Previous executor identifies a completed result from the context you just stepped. Click a row to inspect full values and copy its value or path. Missing targets, unset scores, and failed reads have distinct statuses; use Retry to read again.
codon.ui.help.changes.title: Changed this pause
codon.ui.help.changes.body: Codon compares observed entity scores, entity NBT, and storage NBT between pauses, even without saved watches. The first observation establishes a baseline. Later changes appear in Watches; use their pin to keep watching a field. This covers captured entities and values, not every change in the world.
codon.ui.help.watch_live.title: Live reads and recorded history
codon.ui.help.watch_live.body: Watch and NBT reads are available while paused. Recorded command contexts do not restore old entity data; return to Current for live context reads. During a quick refresh, the previous display may remain briefly before an ellipsis appears. A loading indicator or an old displayed value is not a newly read result.
codon.ui.help.nbt.title: Explore entity NBT
codon.ui.help.nbt.body: Select a live entity context to browse NBT in the inspector. Expand compound and list fields, then scroll to load additional pages automatically. Hover a field for its path and preview, or use Refresh NBT when offered. Recorded or historical contexts do not provide a fresh live NBT tree.
codon.ui.help.nbt_pin.title: Pin fields directly from NBT
codon.ui.help.nbt_pin.body: Left-click a field pin to add or remove a watch for that entity. Right-click to add that path for all available entity contexts, or remove those watches if all are already pinned. Pinned fields stay in Watches when you select another context. Unsupported paths cannot be pinned.
codon.ui.help.saving.title: Saved watches
codon.ui.help.saving.body: Watch definitions are saved with the world for your player and restored when you return. If the Watches window reports Session only or Saving failed, the changes are available for this session but have not been saved. Use Retry saving watches to try again.
